sphere_commentary.overview:
Across 1,000 outcome scores, the three series converge on a core finding: the library produces broadly positive outcomes (means 6.59-6.98) but with series-specific variance patterns reflecting design intent.
• HEALING carries the largest sample (n=574) and tightest performance band (std=1.77), consistent with DESCENT regulatory protocols.
• THRIVING achieves the highest peak scores (T-FC-L3: 7.63) but also higher variance in focus protocols.
• TRANSFORMING shows the widest spread (std=1.87) and lowest aggregate mean, with notable outliers in both directions.
• AutoGluon feature importance highlights avg_view_percentage (0.277) and avg_view_duration (0.221) as top predictors — engagement signals outweigh static protocol parameters.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The series reveal distinct efficacy profiles shaped by protocol type and movement arc.
• HEALING: DESCENT protocols cluster tightly (6.35-7.22), with crisis entries scoring lowest — structurally expected for acute-distress entry points.
• THRIVING: HOLD protocols show a clear level-escalation pattern in Focus & Clarity (L1=6.46, L2=7.19, L3=7.63), suggesting deeper hold phases reward experienced listeners.
• TRANSFORMING: ASCENT protocols produce the widest outcome range (5.7-7.15), with Motivation & Drive entries carrying the lowest positive rates (43-45% pct_pos) in the dataset — a primary development focus.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Multiple protocols show patterns that diverge from series design intent and warrant targeted investigation.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.7, std=2.45) is the clear outlier — lowest mean and highest variance across all protocols, with possible bimodal response distribution.
• T-FC-L3 shows polarization: despite the highest THRIVING mean (7.63), std=1.97 with 10 responses at score 10 versus sparse mid-range — suggests a responder subgroup rather than normal distribution.
• T-FC-L1 receives the most 'slightly busy' rhythm feedback (9/23) in the Focus series — this perceptual signal may explain its underperformance versus L2/L3.
• AutoGluon predicts X-ME-L1 at 8.230 but observed mean is 6.74 — a 1.49-point gap representing either model overfit to engagement features or undiscovered efficacy in a subpopulation.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Four convergent signals emerge across observed outcomes, qualitative data, and AutoGluon predictions.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.7) — Cosmos is significantly underperforming all L3 entries; review Hz depth and descent arc parameters, and investigate whether the listener population for Mind & Clarity requires a gentler entrainment curve.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MD-L1/X-MD-L2 — Motivation & Drive ASCENT entries are the poorest-performing zone (pct_pos 45% and 43%); consider adjusting ascent steepness or starting Hz, and evaluate whether these listeners arrive in states too low for the current arc design.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L1 (n=41, mean=6.46) — receives the most 'slightly busy' rhythm feedback (9/23) among Focus protocols; reduce rhythmic density at L1 entry level to improve entrainment.
• AutoGluon flags X-ME-L1 as a top performer across five zones (score=8.230); this broad cross-bucket potential suggests L2 variant development for Mood & Energy would capture underserved demand.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Analytical framing has shifted substantially between runs, with several protocols showing notable drift.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: X-MD-L3 shows the strongest analytical instability (sim=0.507), followed by H-SL-L1 (0.530) and T-FC-L3 (0.532) — 15 protocols fall below 0.75 similarity, suggesting evolving data patterns or interpretation.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Within-category pairs cluster tightly (T-FC-L1↔L2 at 0.878, H-SL-L1↔L2 at 0.869), while H-OS-L3, T-FC-L3, and T-CF-L3 are the most analytically isolated protocols — they produce distinctive response patterns that don't align with series peers.
• Confidence note: drift readings are based on 2-4 runs per protocol and should be treated as early directional signals rather than stable characterizations.
